label: Bible Study
prompt: Behold, I stand at the _____, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
verse: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
note: Spoken to lukewarm Laodicea — Jesus knocking, waiting for the latch to lift.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: But the very hairs of your head are all _____.
verse: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
note: God's attention to detail extends to your hairline — every strand is numbered, even the ones leaving.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it _____ out Jonah upon the dry land.
verse: And the LORD spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land.
note: Three days inside, then an unceremonious exit: the fish vomited Jonah out onto dry land.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth _____ me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
verse: And the king said unto Araunah, Nay; but I will surely buy it of thee at a price: neither will I offer burnt offerings unto the LORD my God of that which doth cost me nothing. So David bought the threshingfloor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.
note: David refused a free threshing floor for his sacrifice — the same site where Solomon would later build the temple.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: For we are his _____, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
verse: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
note: 'Workmanship' translates the Greek poiema — the root of our word 'poem.' You're God's handiwork.
